The regain cap after a re-establishment and the return cap at and after the end of the return steps rise by one set only after a week whose last executed exposure of the exercise, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), did its whole count (its count before the phase reduction) after its time fit; "an executed exposure" in R7A-SSCTR-r2 condition 9 means this exposure (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1).
A time fit stays a non-reduction for the phase reading and for the return ceiling (R20); a fatigue or phase reduction of the last executed exposure holds the cap (FR2, QE-R7A-22) (met).
A row written before R7-A, which states no counts, reads its week’s planned counts, so every representation reads the same (met).

D57 (required before any freeze is accepted; not met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): a cap ends only after a week whose last executed exposure did its whole count after its time fit, and only when the cap is at or above the count the exercise would otherwise have next week, its normal count including any block-boundary set earned at that transition (phase reductions on top). No count after a re-establishment or a return exceeds the largest count executed since then by more than one set, at block boundaries too. At R7A1-FREEZE-A1 the return cap ends against the ending week’s normal count and after weeks fitted below their whole count (ssctr-r7a1-grid.mjs: 38 counts two sets above the largest executed since the return, 1 to 3; 8 return-cap ends after weeks whose every exposure was fitted below), so this clause is outside the approval until a later freeze meets it. Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold.

D58 (required before any freeze is accepted; not met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): in a short return the first quality slot after the break is the first quality slot still ahead of the return report, in the week re-entry starts or a later week; it runs easy, recorded as an adaptation of the week that holds it so a later re-plan and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed. S5 (C5): a session dated before a return reported the same week is never moved into the re-entry and never counts as done in next week’s conditional plan; a lift not done since the break starts at the return entry (strengthEntrySets at RIR at least strengthEntryMinimumRir), never at a later step without an entry; a newer report of a break that began this week starts from the start the week had before an earlier report of it, so a corrected report plans the week as the corrected report alone (met).

S6 (C3): once the week is complete, its evidence decides next week’s start whatever handler re-plans (an unreported complete week holds); while the week is under way, the conditional plan of the week as now planned decides, its rows assumed executed as prescribed except sessions dated before a return; a return’s re-base of next week is kept; the weekly review re-derives the start from evidence (met).

S6 (run ceiling): in a conditional projection the earlier projected weeks count as executed for the single-run ceiling, as the policy states; the first week a review projects uses completed runs only (met).

S9 (C5): an event change re-plans this week’s remaining days when it moves one of them into or out of the taper, race-window or post-event days, by days to the race; completed sessions stay as executed; only the taper of the event in force remains; the race statement stays the longest continuous run planned before the race (met).

S10 (C4): content an adaptation moves into a slot keeps the week’s earlier adaptations, each with its own clock; a move never uses a skipped slot; a systemic fatigue report with nothing left to reduce reviews the week with its signal and records it, so a later review of the same week keeps it; a mid-week reduction does not set that signal (met).

S10 (C2): a change stated from a later date applies from the first week that begins on or after it, starting that week from the week before it as planned with its transition under the new context (met).

S8: the first strength week after a break stays RETURN_ENTRY with the run in RETURN mode whatever change of the same evening comes first; a moved race leaves one race; a reviewed transition survives a later equipment change; same-week adaptations survive an event change (met).

The regain base is the re-establishment count before its phase reduction: min(goal sets for the role, 2, the count the exercise would otherwise have that day). A re-establishment reduced by its phase is followed by that count itself, as a phase-reduced return step 2 is followed by the step-2 count (Q1, reading A).

The cap rises by one set only after a week whose last executed exposure of the exercise executed its whole count (executed sets equal to its count before the phase reduction, gate ADVANCE or EARNED, a logged set); a week whose executed row was below that count, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, never raises it. A phase week whose reduction did not bring the row below that count counts as a whole executed week.
Every later count stays at or below the cap, with phase reductions on top, and is never more than one set above the largest count executed since the re-establishment.

At a re-establishment the load stays effort-guided under the earlier ceiling; no load increase, new exercise or rotation in taper or race week.
The final validation rejects any strength row above its day phase dose or below the phase minimum reps in reserve, whatever branch built it.

S2: on HOLD and REGRESS a log that confirms the known load leaves the repetition target as planned (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); on ADVANCE or EARNED the logged repetitions may replace it; a newly established load (first establishment or re-establishment by effort) is adopted with the repetitions logged for it. A set without repetitions is unknown, never a missed target.

S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold. D58 (not met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): in a short return the first quality slot after the break is the first quality slot still ahead of the return report, in the week re-entry starts or a later week; it runs easy, recorded as an adaptation of the week that holds it so a later re-plan and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed. At R7A1-FREEZE-A1 the rule reaches only the week re-entry starts: when that week’s quality slot is already past and two or more sessions remain, next week’s first quality slot keeps its quality dose (ssctr-r7a1-short.mjs: 96 of 315 cases, also after the weekly review; in a 10-day break THRESHOLD 41 where the last executed was 34), so this clause is outside the approval until a later freeze meets it. Regression: the short grid’s defects at 0 after the return and after the review.

S4/S9: when an event change moves any remaining day of the current week into or out of the taper, race-window or post-event days, or the race itself is still ahead this week, those days are re-planned under the new phases by days to the race (proximitySemantics), with completed sessions unchanged; a goal change that only renames a training phase applies from the next week.

S5: a missed session is moved only to a later chosen day of the same sport, in the same day phase, where every strength row keeps its kind on the new date (a known or from-log row never becomes a re-establishment by moving, nor the reverse); otherwise it is skipped without debt.

S6: a fatigue reduction lowers the recorded count and makes the week reduced; the return ceiling is the largest whole count executed that week outside a phase reduction, each exposure counted after its time fit (R20).

D56 (final formulation, R7A1-SSCTR-r1 S1): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when the last executed exposure of the exercise that week, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), executed its count before the phase reduction after its time fit. Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; not met for the end of the return cap (D57). D57 (not met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): see R7A1-SSCTR-D56-FORMULATION.
S7: a week planned as a return-entry week stays one when its remaining days are rebuilt; every new exercise in it gets the entry dose in every time budget and follows the return steps.
